sections.overview: Trogonophis wiegmanni is a burrowing amphisbaenian native to the Maghreb.
sections.identification: Its elongated, limbless body and small eyes beneath the skin suit an underground life.
sections.habitat: It occupies soil beneath stones and other ground cover, as well as some cultivated and open habitats.
sections.diet: A study of one Chafarinas Islands population found insect larvae, snails, isopods, beetles and ants in its diet.
sections.behavior: It spends much of its time burrowing through soil and sheltering under stones.
sections.reproduction: It is ovoviviparous; females give birth to a small litter of two to five young.
sections.ecology: It is endemic to the Maghreb, from Morocco through northern Algeria to northwestern Tunisia.
sections.conservation: The IUCN account lists it as Least Concern, but that global assessment dates from 2008.
